This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. tools.description:

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash

cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.

- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

216	### 4.3 为什么 GPU 构建必须 --release
217	
218	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
219	
220	README 的表述毫不含糊：**「Always use `--release` for GPU builds.」**（[../README.md:L68](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L68)）。
221	
222	直觉层面的原因：推理引擎的性能热点有两块——GPU kernel 和**主机侧的调度循环**（批组装、KV 簿记、token 拷贝、每 step 的状态机推进）。debug 构建对后者是灾难：
223	
224	1. **无优化**：Rust 代码不内联、不做边界检查消除，调度循环慢一到两个数量级；
225	2. **调试开销**：dev profile 默认开启 `debug-assertions` 和整数溢出检查，热循环里每次索引、每次算术都多付钱；
226	3. GPU 每一步都在等主机喂活，主机慢 → 整条流水线慢 → 常见结局是"看起来卡死/超时"，而不是"慢一点但能跑"。

228	两个容易忽略的边界：

231	- 测试同样要 release：README「Development」一节的示例测试命令全部带 `--release`（[../README.md:L208-L218](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L208-L218)），"Run checks in release mode"。

282	### 4.4 jemalloc 全局分配器
283	
284	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
285	
286	- 先给不熟悉的读者一句话：`#[global_allocator]` 是 Rust 的一个语言级挂钩——把一个实现了 `GlobalAlloc` trait 的 static 标注上去，进程内所有默认堆分配（`Vec`、`Box`、`String`……）就都走它。
287	- 本项目在**非 msvc 平台**把全局分配器换成了 jemalloc（[src/main.rs:L20-L22](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L20-L22)）。
288	- **通用工程理由**（诚实标注：仓库源码和文档都没有为这个选择写注释或基准，以下是社区通行解释，不是仓库声明的事实）：一个长期运行、多线程的 serving 进程会持续产生大量小对象分配（每请求的 token 缓冲、事件、状态结构）。glibc 的 ptmalloc2 在多线程下锁竞争与碎片更明显；jemalloc 的 per-thread arena + tcache 能降低竞争、抑制碎片。Windows 的 MSVC 工具链没有可用的 jemallocator 移植，所以用 `cfg` 门排除，回落到系统分配器。
289	- 一个值得记住的工程细节：这个开关**成对出现在两处**——`Cargo.toml` 的 target 依赖（控制"依赖是否编译"）和 `main.rs` 的 cfg static（控制"代码是否存在"）。两侧用同一个条件 `not(target_env = "msvc")` 保持一致。
290	
291	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
292	
293	```text
294	编译期（目标平台判定）:
295	  Linux/macOS（非 msvc）
296	    ├─ Cargo.toml: tikv-jemallocator 进入依赖图
297	    └─ main.rs:    static GLOBAL 存在，带 #[global_allocator]
298	         → 进程所有默认堆分配走 jemalloc
299	  Windows MSVC
300	    ├─ Cargo.toml: 依赖不存在
301	    └─ main.rs:    static 被 cfg 掉
302	         → 使用 MSVC 系统分配器
303	
304	运行期:
305	  任意 Vec/String/Box 分配 → GLOBAL.alloc() → jemalloc
306	```
307	
308	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
309	
310	- [Cargo.toml:L31-L32](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L31-L32) — target 依赖段：`[target.'cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))'.dependencies]` 下的 `tikv-jemallocator = "0.6"`。注意它与上面 `[dependencies]` 段的分界——这行只在非 msvc 目标上生效，且**不是** optional：不需要 feature 开关，平台符合就编。
311	- [src/main.rs:L20-L22](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L20-L22) — 与依赖段条件完全相同的 `#[cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))]` 守卫 + `#[global_allocator]` 标注的 `static GLOBAL: tikv_jemallocator::Jemalloc`。这三行就是整个机制的全部代码；jemalloc 以库的形式被静态链入，无任何运行时配置。

368	- **--release**：主机侧调度循环未优化 + 调试断言开销会让 GPU 流水线拖垮，README 明示 GPU 构建与测试都必须 release；nvcc 侧优化不受 cargo profile 控制。
369	- **jemalloc**：非 msvc 平台经两处成对的 `cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))`（依赖 + `#[global_allocator]` static）把全局分配器换成 jemalloc；这是通用工程选择，仓库未附专门说明。
370	- **验证手段**：`cargo tree -e features` 看 feature 图、`cargo metadata --no-deps` 看包身份、`--version` 看运行时自报——三者都不需要读模型代码。
371	
372	## 7. 下一步学习建议
373	
374	构建只是入口。下一讲（u1-l3「main.rs 全景」）将走进 `main()` 本体：`ModelLineRegistry::new` → `build_command` → 读 `config.json` → `detect` → 两级 `validate` → `serve_plan` → `spawn_blocking` 加载引擎 → 三条 serve 分支的选择。建议提前通读 [src/main.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L146-L289) 的 `main()` 函数，并留意本讲已见过的两处伏笔：`model_lines()` 如何被注册表消费、`--version` 所在的 clap 命令如何被 `build_command` 扩展。检测门（`detect` 与 `feature_gate_hint`）的完整机制则在第 4 讲展开。

# 构建与运行：feature 矩阵、--release 与全局分配器

> 学习手册 · 单元一（入门）· 第 2 讲 · 依赖第 1 讲「项目定位与架构地图」

## 1. 本讲目标

上一讲我们建立了全局地图：`pegainfer-server` 是一个约 300 行的纯分发二进制，模型逻辑全部住在各自的模型 crate 里。本讲回答一个更具体的问题：**同一个 `src/main.rs`，为什么能编译出"只支持 Qwen3"和"支持 Kimi-K2"两种完全不同的二进制？**

学完本讲你应该能够：

1. 解释 Cargo feature 如何决定二进制内容：`default = ["qwen3"]`，其余模型线经 `--features` 拉入对应 crate；能读懂「拉入依赖」与「同时转发 crate 内部 feature」两种写法的差异。
2. 说出二进制名 `pegainfer`、包名 `pegainfer-server`、CLI 自报的版本号分别来自 `Cargo.toml` 与 `main.rs` 的哪些字段和哪一行代码。
3. 说明为什么 GPU 构建必须 `--release`、为什么非 msvc 平台用 jemallocator 做全局分配器。
4. 会用 `cargo tree -e features` 与 `--version` 验证自己的 feature 构建假设，而不是靠猜。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言把四个概念先过一遍，已熟悉的读者可以跳到源码地图。

- **Cargo feature（特性）**：Cargo 的编译期开关。一个 feature 就是一个名字，打开它等价于"启用一组编译期配置"——最常见的是把某个 `optional = true` 的依赖拉进编译图。feature 只在编译时存在，运行时没有"开关"这回事：没编译进去的代码就是不存在。
- **optional dependency（可选依赖）**：在 `[dependencies]` 里声明为 `optional = true`（本 crate 经 workspace 依赖 + feature 表达成）的依赖默认**不编译**。只有当某个 feature 用 `dep:包名` 指名激活它，或用户直接 `--features 包名` 时，它才进入编译图。
- **debug 与 release 构建**：`cargo build`（默认 dev profile）不做优化、开启调试断言和整数溢出检查；`cargo build --release` 做优化并关掉这些检查。对普通 CLI 两者只差几倍速度，对每个 token 都要跑一遍调度循环的推理引擎，差距会放大到不可用。
- **全局分配器（global allocator）**：Rust 里 `Box`/`Vec`/`String` 等所有堆分配默认走"系统分配器"。用一个 `#[global_allocator]` 标注的 static，可以把整个进程的默认分配器换成别的实现——本讲的主角是 jemalloc。

构建前提（README「Build from source」一节）：使用仓库钉住的 Rust 工具链（[rust-toolchain.toml](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/rust-toolchain.toml#L1-L4)，`nightly-2026-07-10`），装好带 `nvcc` 和 cuBLAS 的 CUDA Toolkit。默认的 Qwen3 构建**全程不需要 Python**。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 本讲关注点 |
| --- | --- |
| [Cargo.toml](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L1-L52) | 全部三个最小模块的落点：`[features]` 矩阵、`[[bin]]` 与 `default-run`、jemalloc 的 target 依赖 |
| [src/main.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L1-L60) | 与 feature 表互为镜像的 `model_lines()`、`#[global_allocator]`、clap 的 `--version` 装配 |
| [../README.md](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L57-L68) | 「Build from source」与「Always use --release」的官方表述 |
| [../Cargo.toml](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/Cargo.toml#L1-L3)（工作区根） | `default-members = ["pegainfer-server"]`——仓库根目录直接 `cargo run` 的原因 |
| [../rust-toolchain.toml](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/rust-toolchain.toml#L1-L4) | 钉住的 nightly 工具链 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 feature 矩阵：default = qwen3，其余按需拉入

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

PegaInfer 支持多条模型线（Qwen3、Qwen3.5、Gemma 4、DeepSeek-V2-Lite、Kimi-K2、GLM-5.2、Kimi-K3……），但没有一个二进制包含全部。设计是：**每个模型 crate 都是 `pegainfer-server` 的可选依赖，一条模型线对应一个同名 feature**。

这样做的直接收益（上一讲已建立，这里从构建视角再看一遍）：

- 出厂二进制只含 Qwen3：体积小、构建期不需要 Python/Triton；
- 用户按需 `--features kimi-k2` 重建，才把 Kimi-K2 的权重加载、调度器和 Marlin INT4 内核编进来；
- 不需要的模型线的代码**根本不参与编译**，而不是"编译了但运行时不用"。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

以 `cargo run --release --features gemma4` 为例，从命令到"二进制认识 Gemma 4"的完整链条：

```text
cargo run --release --features gemma4
  │
  ├─ 1. cargo 解析 feature：gemma4 = ["dep:pegainfer-gemma4",
  │                                  "pegainfer-gemma4/gemma4"]
  │
  ├─ 2. 可选依赖 pegainfer-gemma4 被激活 → 进入编译图
  │      同时它在模型 crate 内部的同名 feature "gemma4" 被打开
  │      （内核面归线自己的 feature 拥有）
  │
  ├─ 3. main.rs 中 #[cfg(feature = "gemma4")] 守卫的
  │      &pegainfer_gemma4::model_line::MODEL_LINE 这一行存在
  │      → 注册进 model_lines() 向量
  │
  └─ 4. 运行时 detect 才有机会认领 Gemma 4 的 config.json
```

不加 `--features` 时，第 2、3 步整体消失：`model_lines()` 向量里没有这一项，`detect` 永远不会认领 Gemma 4 的配置——这就是"被编译掉"的确切含义。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看 feature 表本体：

- [Cargo.toml:L34-L48](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L34-L48) — `[features]` 段。第 36 行 `default = ["qwen3"]`：不加任何参数构建时只启用 qwen3；第 35 行的注释点明设计意图「Qwen3-4B is the default model line: pure Rust + CUDA, no Python at build time」。
- 注意两种写法的差异。第 37 行 `qwen3 = ["dep:pegainfer-qwen3"]` **只拉入依赖**；第 42 行 `gemma4 = ["dep:pegainfer-gemma4", "pegainfer-gemma4/gemma4"]` 在拉入依赖之外，**还要打开模型 crate 内部的同名 feature**。从写法就能读出：gemma4（以及 glm52、k3、kimi-k2、deepseek-v2-lite、qwen35）的内核面挂在自己 crate 的 feature 后面，需要显式转发；qwen3、qwen4 拉入依赖本身就够了。
- 第 46-47 行 `qwen35` 的注释是构建期要求的重要信号：`# Qwen3.5 pulls in the Triton AOT kernels (Python + Triton at build time).` —— 想构建 qwen35，先准备好带 Triton 的 Python 环境。

可选依赖的声明在依赖段里：

- [Cargo.toml:L18-L26](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L18-L26) — 七个模型 crate（deepseek-v2-lite、gemma4、glm52、k3、kimi-k2、qwen3、qwen35、qwen4 共八个条目）全部带 `optional = true`。对照第 14-16 行的 `anyhow`、`clap`、`log`：它们没有 optional，是任何构建都必需的骨架。

代码侧的镜像是 `model_lines()`：

- [src/main.rs:L24-L43](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L24-L43) — 每个条目前面都有 `#[cfg(feature = "...")]` 守卫。feature 关掉时该行代码不存在；又因为依赖也没编译，两侧互相印证、不会出现"引用了不存在的 crate"的编译错误。这个函数就是 feature 矩阵在源码里的唯一落点——`main.rs` 其余部分对模型线一无所知。

README 对这套机制的官方表述：

- [../README.md:L142-L144](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L142-L144) — 「Only **`qwen3`** is enabled by default... Build other lines with `--features <feature>`」，并说明启动时由 `--model-path` 指向的 checkpoint 的 `config.json` 识别模型家族（检测门的细节是第 4 讲的主题）。
- [../README.md:L73-L80](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L73-L80) — Qwen3.5 的构建步骤：`uv venv` + 装 triton + `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON=.venv/bin/python`，再 `cargo run --release --features qwen35`。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：不读一行模型代码，用 `cargo tree` 证明「默认构建编入了哪些线、`--features` 如何把可选依赖点亮」。

**操作步骤**（在工作区根目录执行；`cargo tree` 只做依赖解析，不编译代码，纯 CPU 环境即可）：

```bash
cd <仓库根目录>

# 1) 默认 feature 集的依赖图（含 feature 边）
cargo tree -p pegainfer-server -e features > /tmp/server-default.txt

# 2) 加 gemma4 后的依赖图
cargo tree -p pegainfer-server -e features --features gemma4 > /tmp/server-gemma4.txt

# 3) 对比两份图
diff /tmp/server-default.txt /tmp/server-gemma4.txt
```

**需要观察的现象**：

- 默认图中应出现 `pegainfer-qwen3` 节点（经由 `default` → `qwen3` → `dep:pegainfer-qwen3` 这条 feature 链），且**没有** `pegainfer-gemma4`；
- 加 `--features gemma4` 后，diff 的增量里应出现 `pegainfer-gemma4` 节点及其 `gemma4` feature 边。

**预期结果**：你能指出 optional dependency 被激活的准确位置——不是运行时判断，而是依赖图里多了一个节点。图中具体行的措辞随 cargo 版本略有差异，以「`pegainfer-gemma4` 字样是否出现」为准。**待本地验证**（本讲义撰写环境未执行 cargo）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：出厂（stock）二进制为什么无法服务 Kimi-K2 的 checkpoint？用户会看到什么？

答案：`default = ["qwen3"]` 未启用 `kimi-k2`，`pegainfer-kimi-k2` 是 optional 依赖、没进编译图，`model_lines()` 里没有对应条目，运行时 `detect` 得到 `NoMatch`；由于 `kimi_k25` 属于已知家族，`feature_gate_hint` 会附加提示 rebuild with `--features kimi-k2`（提示机制的精读在第 4 讲）。

**练习 2**：`qwen35` 与 `qwen3` 的 feature 定义差在一处转发（`"pegainfer-qwen35/qwen35"`），这个转发在构建期意味着什么？

答案：它打开 `pegainfer-qwen35` crate 内部的同名 feature，而那条线挂着 Triton AOT 内核生成——所以构建 qwen35 需要带 Triton 的 Python（`PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON`）；qwen3 的定义只拉依赖，因此默认构建可以做到全程无 Python。

**练习 3**：如果把 `--features kimi-k2` 拼错成 `--features kimi_k2`，会发生什么？

答案：cargo 直接报 unknown feature 错误、构建失败。feature 名是编译期契约，不存在"静默忽略"——这也是为什么 `model_lines()` 的 cfg 守卫字符串和 feature 表必须逐字符一致。

### 4.2 二进制的身份：[[bin]]、default-run 与 --version

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

三个容易混淆的名字要分开：

| 名字 | 值 | 来源 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 包名（crate 名） | `pegainfer-server` | `Cargo.toml` 的 `[package] name` |
| 产物二进制名 | `pegainfer` | `Cargo.toml` 的 `[[bin]] name` |
| CLI 自报的家门 | `pegainfer 0.1.1` | `main.rs` 里 `clap::Command::new("pegainfer")` + 编译期版本宏 |

包名与二进制名**故意不同**：crate 在 workspace 里叫 `pegainfer-server`（职责清晰），用户敲的命令是 `pegainfer`（短、好装到 PATH 上）。`[[bin]]` 就是这次改名的落点。`default-run` 则回答"这个包有多个 bin 时 `cargo run` 选哪个"——本包目前只有一个 bin，它是防漂移的显式声明：将来若加入第二个 bin，`cargo run` 的行为不会悄悄改变。

`--version` 的输出来自两处代码的配合：名字是 `clap::Command::new("pegainfer")` 的字面量，版本号是 `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`——一个编译期宏，取的就是 `[package] version = "0.1.1"`。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

在仓库根目录执行 `cargo run --release -- --version` 的解析链：

```text
仓库根目录（虚拟 workspace，无 [package]）
  │
  ├─ 1. cargo 需要知道运行哪个包
  │      → 根 Cargo.toml: default-members = ["pegainfer-server"]
  │
  ├─ 2. 该包内选哪个 bin
  │      → pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml: [[bin]] name = "pegainfer"（default-run 同名）
  │
  ├─ 3. 编译并运行 target/release/pegainfer --version
  │
  └─ 4. clap 打印 "<name> <version>"
         → name 来自 Command::new("pegainfer")
         → version 来自 env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") = "0.1.1"
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

- [Cargo.toml:L1-L11](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L1-L11) — `[package]` 段：第 6 行 `name = "pegainfer-server"`（包名）、第 7 行 `version = "0.1.1"`（`--version` 的最终来源）、第 3 行 `default-run = "pegainfer"`；第 9-11 行 `[[bin]]` 把产物命名为 `pegainfer`、指向 `src/main.rs`。
- [src/main.rs:L152-L156](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L152-L156) — `main()` 里构建 clap 命令：第 153 行 `clap::Command::new("pegainfer")` 决定 `--version`/`--help` 里显示的程序名；第 154 行 `.version(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))` 把包版本注入。clap 默认的 `--version` 输出格式就是「名字 + 空格 + 版本」。
- [../Cargo.toml:L1-L3](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/Cargo.toml#L1-L3) — 工作区根是虚拟 manifest，第 2 行 `default-members = ["pegainfer-server"]`。没有这一行，根目录的 `cargo run` 会直接报错（cargo 不知道运行哪个包）；有了它，README 里根目录一键 `cargo run --release -- --model-path ...` 才成立。

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：把「三个名字」各自钉到具体字段/代码行上，验证你对自己构建产物的假设。

**操作步骤**：

```bash
# 1) 无需编译即可读取包元数据（纯 CPU、秒级）
cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq '.packages[] | select(.name=="pegainfer-server") | {name, version, binaries: [.bins[].name]}'

# 2) 有 CUDA 环境时，真正构建并询问版本（首次构建耗时较长）
cargo run --release -- --version

# 3) 确认产物文件名
ls -la target/release/pegainfer
```

**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**：

- 步骤 1 应返回 `name: "pegainfer-server"`、`version: "0.1.1"`、`binaries: ["pegainfer"]`——包名与 bin 名不同、版本来自 `[package]`；
- 步骤 2 预期输出一行 `pegainfer 0.1.1`（clap 的标准 version 输出格式）；
- 步骤 3 确认磁盘上的文件叫 `pegainfer` 而不是 `pegainfer-server`。

**待本地验证**（本讲义撰写环境未执行 cargo；步骤 2 需要完整 CUDA 工具链）。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`--version` 输出里的字符串 `pegainfer` 来自哪一行代码？来自 `[[bin]] name` 吗？

答案：来自 [src/main.rs:L153](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L153) 的 `clap::Command::new("pegainfer")` 字面量。`[[bin]] name` 只决定产物文件名，不影响 CLI 自报的家门——两者目前一致，靠人工保持同步。

**练习 2**：为什么在仓库根目录直接 `cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B` 就能启动服务，而不需要 `-p pegainfer-server`？

答案：工作区根是虚拟 manifest，[../Cargo.toml:L2](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/Cargo.toml#L2) 的 `default-members = ["pegainfer-server"]` 把默认运行目标指定为本包；包内再由 `default-run = "pegainfer"` 选中唯一的 bin。

**练习 3**：把 `[package] version` 改成 `0.2.0` 并重新构建后，`--version` 输出如何变化？为什么？

答案：输出变为 `pegainfer 0.2.0`。`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` 是编译期宏，在编译时读取包版本并烧进二进制，所以必须重新编译才能看到变化。

### 4.3 为什么 GPU 构建必须 --release

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

README 的表述毫不含糊：**「Always use `--release` for GPU builds.」**（[../README.md:L68](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L68)）。

直觉层面的原因：推理引擎的性能热点有两块——GPU kernel 和**主机侧的调度循环**（批组装、KV 簿记、token 拷贝、每 step 的状态机推进）。debug 构建对后者是灾难：

1. **无优化**：Rust 代码不内联、不做边界检查消除，调度循环慢一到两个数量级；
2. **调试开销**：dev profile 默认开启 `debug-assertions` 和整数溢出检查，热循环里每次索引、每次算术都多付钱；
3. GPU 每一步都在等主机喂活，主机慢 → 整条流水线慢 → 常见结局是"看起来卡死/超时"，而不是"慢一点但能跑"。

两个容易忽略的边界：

- `--release` 改变的是 **Rust 主机代码**的编译档位；CUDA 侧的 `.cu` 由 `pegainfer-kernels` 的 `build.rs` 调 `nvcc` 编译，其优化参数不走 cargo 的 profile 开关；
- 测试同样要 release：README「Development」一节的示例测试命令全部带 `--release`（[../README.md:L208-L218](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L208-L218)），"Run checks in release mode"。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

dev 与 release 两个 profile 的关键差异（Cargo 默认值，本仓库未覆写这两个 profile）：

| 维度 | dev（默认） | release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `opt-level` | 0（不优化） | 3 |
| `debug-assertions` | 开 | 关 |
| `overflow-checks` | 开 | 关 |
| 对引擎的意义 | 每 step 的调度/簿记代码慢 10-100 倍，GPU 等主机 | 主机侧跟得上 GPU |

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

- [../README.md:L57-L68](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L57-L68) — 官方构建步骤：`export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda` 后 `cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B`；第 68 行就是那句「Always use --release」。同时说明本 crate 是 server 入口、模型实现在各模型 crate。
- [../README.md:L208-L211](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/README.md#L208-L211) — 单元测试也用 `cargo test --release --workspace --lib`，理由同源：含 GPU/张量逻辑的测试在 debug 下会慢到超时。
- [../rust-toolchain.toml:L1-L4](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/rust-toolchain.toml#L1-L4) — 仓库钉住 `nightly-2026-07-10`（含 rustfmt、clippy）。`edition = "2024"`（[Cargo.toml:L4](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L4)）也依赖较新的编译器——构建前不要随意切换工具链。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用「编译时间」这个不依赖 GPU 的指标，直观感受两个 profile 的差异（产物优化路径完全不同）。

**操作步骤**：

```bash
# 1) 清理后各做一次完整默认构建，记录耗时
cargo clean
time cargo build            # dev profile
cargo clean
time cargo build --release  # release profile
```

两个产物分别为 `target/debug/pegainfer` 与 `target/release/pegainfer`，可用 `ls -la` 顺带对比体积。

**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**：两个 profile 的编译时间不同（release 通常更慢，因为要做优化），产物体积差异明显；`target/debug/` 与 `target/release/` 下各有一个名为 `pegainfer` 的可执行文件。**运行性能对比需要 GPU 与模型权重，待本地验证**；在没有 CUDA 的机器上，本实践的编译步骤也可能因 kernels 依赖而失败——此时退化为纯阅读型实践：对照 4.3.2 的表格，向自己复述每个开关对调度循环的影响。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：debug 构建慢，具体慢在哪几层？

答案：主机侧 Rust 调度/簿记代码完全未优化（opt-level=0），叠加默认开启的 `debug-assertions` 与整数溢出检查；GPU 每步依赖主机推进，主机慢导致整条流水线拖垮。

**练习 2**：`--release` 会让 nvcc 把 CUDA kernel 编得更快吗？

答案：不会直接改变。`.cu` 的编译由 `pegainfer-kernels` 的 `build.rs` 调 nvcc 完成，优化参数由那边决定；`--release` 改变的是 Rust 代码（含 build script 自身运行）的档位。

**练习 3**：为什么仓库连单元测试命令都写 `--release`？

答案：测试同样执行引擎/张量逻辑，debug 下慢到容易超时；README「Development」一节的示例（`cargo test --release --workspace --lib` 等）是官方约定的标准跑法。

### 4.4 jemalloc 全局分配器

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

- 先给不熟悉的读者一句话：`#[global_allocator]` 是 Rust 的一个语言级挂钩——把一个实现了 `GlobalAlloc` trait 的 static 标注上去，进程内所有默认堆分配（`Vec`、`Box`、`String`……）就都走它。
- 本项目在**非 msvc 平台**把全局分配器换成了 jemalloc（[src/main.rs:L20-L22](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L20-L22)）。
- **通用工程理由**（诚实标注：仓库源码和文档都没有为这个选择写注释或基准，以下是社区通行解释，不是仓库声明的事实）：一个长期运行、多线程的 serving 进程会持续产生大量小对象分配（每请求的 token 缓冲、事件、状态结构）。glibc 的 ptmalloc2 在多线程下锁竞争与碎片更明显；jemalloc 的 per-thread arena + tcache 能降低竞争、抑制碎片。Windows 的 MSVC 工具链没有可用的 jemallocator 移植，所以用 `cfg` 门排除，回落到系统分配器。
- 一个值得记住的工程细节：这个开关**成对出现在两处**——`Cargo.toml` 的 target 依赖（控制"依赖是否编译"）和 `main.rs` 的 cfg static（控制"代码是否存在"）。两侧用同一个条件 `not(target_env = "msvc")` 保持一致。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
编译期（目标平台判定）:
  Linux/macOS（非 msvc）
    ├─ Cargo.toml: tikv-jemallocator 进入依赖图
    └─ main.rs:    static GLOBAL 存在，带 #[global_allocator]
         → 进程所有默认堆分配走 jemalloc
  Windows MSVC
    ├─ Cargo.toml: 依赖不存在
    └─ main.rs:    static 被 cfg 掉
         → 使用 MSVC 系统分配器

运行期:
  任意 Vec/String/Box 分配 → GLOBAL.alloc() → jemalloc
```

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

- [Cargo.toml:L31-L32](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/Cargo.toml#L31-L32) — target 依赖段：`[target.'cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))'.dependencies]` 下的 `tikv-jemallocator = "0.6"`。注意它与上面 `[dependencies]` 段的分界——这行只在非 msvc 目标上生效，且**不是** optional：不需要 feature 开关，平台符合就编。
- [src/main.rs:L20-L22](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L20-L22) — 与依赖段条件完全相同的 `#[cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))]` 守卫 + `#[global_allocator]` 标注的 `static GLOBAL: tikv_jemallocator::Jemalloc`。这三行就是整个机制的全部代码；jemalloc 以库的形式被静态链入，无任何运行时配置。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践（源码阅读型）

**实践目标**：验证"两处 cfg 成对"这一结构，并推演漂移的后果。

**操作步骤**：

1. 打开上面两个链接，确认两处条件字符串逐字符相同：`not(target_env = "msvc")`；
2. 在工作区根执行反向依赖查询（只解析、不编译）：

```bash
cargo tree -p pegainfer-server -i tikv-jemallocator
```

3. 阅读并回答两个假设问题（不用真改代码）：
   - 若删掉 Cargo.toml 第 31-32 行、保留 main.rs 第 20-22 行，编译会怎样？
   - 反之，保留依赖、cfg 掉 static，又会怎样？

**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**：

- 步骤 2 在 Linux 上应显示 `tikv-jemallocator` 是 `pegainfer-server` 的直接依赖（反向树的根），印证它是被 target 门控引入的顶层选择而非某个库的传递依赖；
- 步骤 3 的答案：前一情形 `tikv_jemallocator` 这个名字解析不到，**编译失败**（依赖不在图里）；后一情形能编译，只是留下一个没被使用的多余依赖。也就是说这对 cfg 的"同步"由编译器单向强制（代码引用依赖），反方向（依赖没代码用）不报错——这正是要靠 review 保持成对的原因。

**待本地验证**（步骤 2 的输出形式；本讲义撰写环境未执行 cargo）。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么这个 cfg 门要写在 Cargo.toml 和 main.rs 两个地方？

答案：Cargo 的 target-specific dependencies 只控制"依赖是否参与编译"，`#[cfg]` 只控制"这段代码是否存在"。要"非 msvc 才有 jemalloc"必须两侧同条件；漂移的后果见上面实践第 3 步——一侧是硬编译错误，另一侧是静默的死依赖。

**练习 2**：换成 jemalloc 后，进程里哪些分配走它？

答案：所有经 Rust 默认分配器的堆分配（`Vec`/`String`/`Box` 等）。本 crate 没有绕开默认分配器的用法；"显式指定其他分配器的库不受影响"是通用边界，不针对本仓库。

**练习 3**：在 Windows MSVC 构建下，运行时内存分配行为与 Linux 构建有何不同？

答案：MSVC 目标上 `tikv-jemallocator` 不进依赖图、`GLOBAL` static 被 cfg 掉，进程使用 MSVC 的系统分配器；二进制中也不含 jemalloc 代码。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：给你的构建画一张"构建画像"。**

把本讲四个模块串成一次可复现的检查，产出半页笔记：

1. **feature 集**：执行 4.1.4 的 `cargo tree` 对比（默认 vs `--features gemma4`），在笔记里记下默认构建激活的模型线（应为 qwen3 一条）与 gemma4 带来的新节点，并用一句话解释 `dep:` 转发链。
2. **二进制身份**：执行 4.2.4 的 `cargo metadata --no-deps` 查询，抄下包名、版本、bin 名三元组；若环境允许再跑 `cargo run --release -- --version`，把实际输出与三元组互相印证，并指出输出中每个字符的来源字段/代码行。
3. **档位与分配器**：在笔记里写下两件事的"为什么"各一句（为什么必须 `--release`；为什么非 msvc 换 jemalloc——并注明后者仓库未附官方理由）。
4. **自检问题**（写进笔记末尾）：如果明天要在这台机器上服务 GLM-5.2，你需要哪条构建命令？提示：从 4.1.3 的 feature 表出发，注意 glm52 行的转发写法与它挂的 TileLang/sm_90a 构建要求（README 环境变量表）。

预期产出：一份能回答"我编的二进制里有什么、叫什么、为什么这么编"的画像笔记。所有 cargo 命令的观察结果**待本地验证**。

## 6. 本讲小结

- **feature 矩阵**：`default = ["qwen3"]`；每条模型线一个 feature，激活 optional 依赖（部分线还要转发 crate 内部同名 feature 以点亮内核面）；`model_lines()` 的 `#[cfg]` 守卫是矩阵在源码里的唯一落点。
- **二进制身份**：包名 `pegainfer-server`、产物名 `pegainfer`（`[[bin]]`）、CLI 自报 `pegainfer 0.1.1`（`clap::Command::new` 字面量 + `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`）；仓库根 `default-members` 让根目录 `cargo run` 直接可用。
- **--release**：主机侧调度循环未优化 + 调试断言开销会让 GPU 流水线拖垮，README 明示 GPU 构建与测试都必须 release；nvcc 侧优化不受 cargo profile 控制。
- **jemalloc**：非 msvc 平台经两处成对的 `cfg(not(target_env = "msvc"))`（依赖 + `#[global_allocator]` static）把全局分配器换成 jemalloc；这是通用工程选择，仓库未附专门说明。
- **验证手段**：`cargo tree -e features` 看 feature 图、`cargo metadata --no-deps` 看包身份、`--version` 看运行时自报——三者都不需要读模型代码。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

构建只是入口。下一讲（u1-l3「main.rs 全景」）将走进 `main()` 本体：`ModelLineRegistry::new` → `build_command` → 读 `config.json` → `detect` → 两级 `validate` → `serve_plan` → `spawn_blocking` 加载引擎 → 三条 serve 分支的选择。建议提前通读 [src/main.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-server/src/main.rs#L146-L289) 的 `main()` 函数，并留意本讲已见过的两处伏笔：`model_lines()` 如何被注册表消费、`--version` 所在的 clap 命令如何被 `build_command` 扩展。检测门（`detect` 与 `feature_gate_hint`）的完整机制则在第 4 讲展开。

schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
